subject.title: security fix(gateway): defend pre-auth device-signature verify against CPU DoS

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's 1024/256 device-handshake protocol caps and pre-auth device-signature rate-limit semantics as the gateway-owned security fix for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77979?
rationale: The patch appears coherent and tested, but it changes a pre-auth security boundary and protocol validation behavior where maintainer/security intent, not automation, should decide the acceptable compatibility and lockout tradeoff.

options.title: Accept This Mitigation
options.body: Approve the current layered schema, shape-check, and limiter approach after gateway/security owner review, then merge if exact-head CI stays green.

options.title: Narrow Before Merge
options.body: Ask the contributor to remove or move the PoC script, adjust the caps, or add current-head WS proof if owners want a smaller public diff or stronger live evidence.

options.title: Replace The Branch
options.body: Close or pause this PR only if maintainers prefer a different gateway-owned mitigation for the same linked issue.

recommendation.title: Accept This Mitigation
recommendation.body: Approve the current layered schema, shape-check, and limiter approach after gateway/security owner review, then merge if exact-head CI stays green.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the central device-auth handshake history and has the strongest current-main provenance for the affected gateway path.
